steps.text: Combine vinegar and steak seasoning in a medium bowl; stir until seasoning is dissolved. Stir in olive oil until combined.
Place pork into a resealable plastic bag, then pour marinade over pork. Squeeze out air and seal the bag; marinate in the refrigerator for 2 hours to overnight.
When ready to cook, preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Place pork into a glass baking dish along with marinade.

Bake in the preheated oven, basting occasionally, until an instant-read thermometer inserted into the center of the tenderloin reaches an internal temperature of 145 degrees F (65 degrees C), about 1 hour.
Let rest for 10 minutes before slicing and serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Balsamic Roasted Pork Loin
raw_recipe.description: This balsamic pork loin uses a simple marinade of balsamic vinegar, steak seasoning, and olive oil to make the most flavorful pork loin.

video.description: An incredibly simple, flavorful roast that needs just four ingredients.

review.reviewBody: Very yummy. I think the variance in reviews between liking it and saying it is too sharp and vinegary could be due to the quality of balsamic vinegar used. Good quality balsamic is so mild you can eat it straight off a spoon and it is almost sweet. Inexpensive balsamic might as well be plain white vinegar. So don't be thrifty on the vinegar quality, you'll only regret it.

Very tasty, and simple. Just a note to the person that gave this a low review but did this in a slow cooker. All slow cookers are not alike, and I think the word slow cooker can be deceiving. I too have had things come out dry in the slow cooker, but usually from cooking to long to where you simply cook the moisture out of the meat. I think timing is so important in the slow cooker, and adding some chicken broth may help some. Chicken broth and pork go great together. I would try this recipe in the oven as it is posted here first, you might be pleasantly surprised. I always follow a recipe to the letter, then make changes based on my likes and dislikes.

The flavor was delicious, but as other reviewers have mentioned, the meat itself is a little tough.
Update: I take it all back. I've tried a few different variation on this recipe now. The meat was only tough when I let it marinate for only two hours. When you leave it overnight or even 2 nights it gets juicy, tender, and delicious. Also, carrots, butternut squash, sweet potatoes, and pretty much any sweet vegetable taste AMAZING roasting along with this dish in its sauce.

Thank you for an amazing recipe!! My husband raved over it and my daughter ate three slices!! I took the advice of others and baked it over sliced sweet onions and some minced garlic for 45 minutes uncovered at 350. It had delicious flavor and was incredibly moist - definitely a keeper!! Thanks for sharing:)

This recipe is delicious exactly as written, but after reading the reviews, I decided to make some additions. I used a 3.5 lb center cut, boneless pork roast. I used 1/3 c of Kirkland brand olive oil and 1/3 c of Kirkland balsamic vinegar. I added 3 large cloves pressed fresh garlic and 1/3 c honey to the marinade, mixed well and put it all in a large ziplock bag. I marinated for just over 24 hrs. That did the trick! Cooked at 350 degrees and it took a little over 2 hrs to reach 160 degrees, using an instant read thermometer inserted into the center. The honey gave it a nice caramelized glaze and the sweetness balanced well with the balsamic vinegar. The garlic gave it extra savory flavor. Don’t leave out the garlic! I sliced a large onion into thick slices and put them in the bottom of the pan, so the roast wouldn’t stick. I used a disposable aluminum baking pan, the size of a rectangle cake pan, for easy clean up. I wouldn’t use a very deep sided pan for this. Low and slow is the way to cook this because it came out so tender, it was heavenly. This is easy to make and you can absolutely serve this to company. Serve with roasted cut up sweet potatoes or baby potatoes. I used some of the pan juices over the meat. This is going into my repertoire for pork dishes! Loved it!

I'm not intimidated by recipes with a lot of prep, and have tried several for pork loin - they all disappointed me; I was not happy with the flavour, or the state of the meat (I usually found it too dry).

I tried this one figuring that with its' simplicity, I had nothing to lose. I added 4 cloves of finely chopped garlic and 1/4 cup of freshly chopped tarragon to the marinade and left it in the fridge for 2 days.

For prep, I placed it on a bed of baby carrots, since other reviewers mentioned it paired well with sweet vegetables, and drizzled the meat with honey. The cooking time and temperature were bang on - 60 minutes/145 degrees. I removed the pork to rest, and gave the carrots another 35 minutes, they were a nice "al dente" when done, and the liquid reduced to a wonderful au jus.

It is the best pork loin I have ever eaten - flavourful, nicely coloured, and filet-mignon tender! I will be making this again, often!

Superb! I added 1/3 cup honey and chopped garlic, marinating for 4 hours. I seared the pork on high heat in a cast iron pan, then roasted it on a glass baking dish on top of a layer of onions, basting every 0-15 minutes. Check the temperature after about 45 minutes... I waited until an hour and it was slightly over (165 F) but was still moist and tender. Served it with roasted diced sweet potatoes and an excellent ZInfandel. The quantities here worked fine for a 5lb pair of tenderloins, and I spooned the marinade over the served pork. Huge hit with our guests.

Delicious!! I added a couple of glugs of Worcestershire because my balsamic vinegar was a little too bright, and it was very tasty. I cooked it on my gas grill indirect heat at 350 for an hour. I also took the marinade, boiled it, then brushed the roast with 15 minutes to go.

Changed it slightly but the base recipie well worth trying. I used a pork loin placed in a cooking bag, then covered it with this marinade/glaze. For the glaze I used 1/2c brown sugar, 1c basalmic vinegar; (and get a good brand as not all are the same), until I try a recipie once I will not use a cheap brand unless I know it has a good flavor profile. To this I add 2 Tbs of a good extra virgin olive oil, 2 rather generous Tbs of stone ground Dijon mustard, salt and pepper to taste, stir together cover pork close bag bake. After an hour I remove the bag and add fresh green onions, a stick of butter, and several very small red potatoes let it cook until finished usually when potatoes are soft. OMG melts in your mouth, the flavors marry well, Thank you for the base recipie as inspiration!

This was OUTSTANDING! But - I think you either need to 1) love balsamic vinegar OR 2) have high quality balsamic. Some reviewers success with cheap balsamic may fit category #1. And so glad! This recipe rocks! My husband does not love so this flavor profile much so I was grateful to have a quality version I received as a Christmas gift last year. This recipe was so simple yet so outstanding I could hardly believe it! Will absolutely make again! My only change (taken from another reviewer) and I think is a MUST! Cut a thick onion, and some thick-cut mushrooms and lay on the bottom of the pan - roast on top. I flipped halfway through cooking - which meant I gave the onions/mushrooms a stir. So amazing I might make again this week! Thank you!!

Made the marinade exactly as is, letting it marinate only around 4 hours. I then followed another reviewers suggestion and placed the loin on a bed of onion slices once it was ready for the oven. Served it for Christmas Eve dinner with homemade cranberry sauce and roasted red potatoes, using the leftover juices to pour over the potatoes. My husband RAVED about it. Will be making this again!

What a great recipe! Pork loin is 1.99/lb and this makes it a delicacy rather than just a budget-friendly option. I marinated for 24 hours, allowed the pork loin to get to room temp and browned on all sides before setting it up for roasting at 350 in my crock pot. It cooked to 145 degrees in 35 minutes and the vegetable were perfectly cooked as well. I can't wait to make it again. Delicious!

Really enjoyed the flavor given by the balsamic vinegar. I marinaded it overnight, and the flavor wasn't overpowering. 30 minutes into the cook time I added 3 sliced Granny Smith Apples which gave a nice touch to the dish.

5 stars for being really tasty, and being so easy to make. Agree with others, since the balsamic vinegar does the heavy-lifting here, high quality vinegar is key. I cut the oil in 1/2 (to reduce WW points - IYKYK) and marinated 6 hours. My husband and I loved this and it’s going into regular rotation. Served with jasmine rice and corn on the cob. Awesome dinner!

I read some of the comments and let it marinate overnight....well turned into 24 hrs. So tender. I lost track of time and cooked it to 160 so it was a bit dry on the small end...but tasty! Will be definitely make again...with a timer! LOL

Delicious exactly as written. Use good quality balsamic vinegar and olive oil and whisk it really well so they combine. For some reason it's usually at the right temperature around 40 to 45 minutes at our home. This is a staple here, we love it!

We liked it, but I used Italian spice instead of thyme. Also- next time I will add a bit of brown sugar- 1/2 TSB to start. But even w/o tasty. BTW - I used a raspberry balsamic from a shop that crafts their own.

Made the recipe as written, just scaling it up by 50% because my pork loin was 3 pounds. I used a homemade beef rub that is pretty unremarkable (seasoning salt, pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, and a little cumin and chili powder). The results were great. It took about 65 minutes to get the pork loin to about 150 degrees F. It was definitely cooked through but still very juicy and well seasoned. The Balsamic vinegar lends a nice and unexpected tang. 5 stars for being delicious yet so darn quick and and easy!
This may not be the best pork recipe on here, but it is definitely worth the effort because it is so easy.
This recipe caught my eye because of the basic ingredients used in it which is always handy. It is easy to make and the pork was tasty and moist. It was a hit and I will make it again.
